title: Shift imbalance detector and autoworkflow hints for on-call planners
author: Priya Kapoor
release_notes: Adds an on-call shift imbalance detector that scores rotation fairness and surface automated workflow hints to rebalance load. Includes a lightweight UI hinting overlay and a scheduler CLI. No breaking API changes.
body:
Summary: This PR introduces a shift imbalance detector and an "autoworkflow" hinting system for on-call planners. The detector analyzes rotation history, alert load, incident severity, and response latency to compute a per-rotator fairness score and an overall imbalance metric. When imbalance exceeds configurable thresholds the system surfaces automated hints (suggested swap candidates, temporary lightening of pager duty, and a prefilled Linear task with recommended actions).

Motivation: teams have asked for measurable, actionable signals to reduce responder burnout and uneven duty distribution (ENG-1987). Current dashboards show raw counts but give no prescriptive guidance. This work aims to: 1) surface when imbalance is material, 2) explain which contributors and shifts cause the signal, and 3) recommend safe, low-friction remediation steps that ops owners can apply.

Design highlights:
- Fairness scoring: combines normalized incident counts, weighted severity, average response time, and recent on-call hours. We apply exponential recency weighting to prioritize recent load and cap individual incident contribution to prevent outliers from skewing scoring.
- Privacy/opt-in: per-org setting. By default the detector runs in "suggestions-only" mode (no emails, no automated reassignment). Teams can enable a "planner-assist" toggle to get prefilled Linear tasks and calendar invites.
- Autoworkflow hints: generated hints include (a) swap suggestions with minimal overlap in on-call availability, (b) suggested temporary relief windows (paired with reduced routing rules), and (c) canned Linear tasks with summary, risk assessment, and next steps. Hints include a confidence score and the top three data points driving the suggestion.
- UX surface: small overlay in the on-call roster view with imbalance badge, a detail flyout that explains the score and a one-click "Create assist task" button that opens a prefilled Linear draft. Also added a CLI for infra and SRE teams to run scans and export CSVs for audits.

Implementation details:
- New modules: src/analysis/imbalance/ (detector, scoring, tests), src/ui/overlays/imbalance_badge.* (React overlay + styles), cli/imbalance_scan (small Go CLI wrapper), integrations/linear/prefill (templating layer), telemetry/metrics (new imbalance.histogram and hint_generated counters).
- Data sources: alert ingestion (slo-toolkit-alerts), rotation logs, PagerDuty webhook samples (sanitized), and response time traces (from tracing-store). We added a limited, cached view for raw events to avoid heavy queries on large orgs.
- Algorithms: implemented a tunable scoring pipeline with configurable weights; default weights chosen after running the detector on historical data from 8 pilot teams.

Ship plan: staged rollout. Feature is behind a feature flag (feature.imbalance_detector). Pilot enabled for three internal teams for two weeks, then opt-in beta for customers.

Backwards compatibility: UI additions are additive. CLI and telemetry are opt-in. No schema changes to existing rotation or alert tables.

Testing: unit tests covering scoring heuristics and edge cases, integration tests simulating a rotation with synthetic incidents, e2e smoke test for the overlay.

Performance: detector run (full org, 5k people, 90 day window) completes in ~11s on staging batch job (within target <20s).

Safety and audit: all generated hints are stored as audit artifacts; we added a redact pipeline for any personally-identifying text included in prefilled tasks.

Rollout checklist included in the PR body.

Related: builds on prior alert fingerprinting work (ENG-1204) to reduce double-counting similar incidents.

Known limitations and future work:
- Current scoring does not fully account for multi-team on-call overlaps; we'll add cross-rotation normalization in a follow-up (ENG-2042).
- We do not auto-apply swaps; that remains manual to prevent accidental coverage gaps.
- The initial UI is intentionally lightweight; more advanced scheduling suggestions will follow.

review_thread: Daniel Kim (2026-02-21): Good direction. Please add a short note describing how exponential recency weighting is parametrized so operators can tune it. Also request a perf test for 10k people orgs.
Priya Kapoor (2026-02-21): Added tuning doc and added a perf job in CI that runs a reduced synthetic load for 10k people. See commit b2d4e6f.
Nina Flores (2026-02-22): Minor UX nit — the badge color should respect high-contrast mode and not rely solely on color. Please add an icon fallback.
Priya Kapoor (2026-02-22): Addressed; added icon and persisted color token. See commit c3f5a7b.
Marcus Li (2026-02-23): Suggest we add a maximum per-rotator cap and document the rationale in scoring docs to prevent aggressive rebalancing in small teams.
Priya Kapoor (2026-02-23): Implemented cap of 4 incidents/month contribution and updated docs. Tests added to assert cap behavior.

Daniel Kim (2026-02-24): CI passed on rerun, approving for canary.
Approval: LGTM (ready to merge after canary monitoring).
